name: ring-spinner
title: Ring Spinner
description: A spinner whose arc stretches as it turns, fills to a known amount, and closes into a check or a cross.

perf.budget: One small Skia canvas driven by one clock on the UI thread while it spins. The clock stops once it shows progress, success or an error.

measurements.notes: The demo upload ring keeps counting, so it draws at rest; a settled spinner stops its clock.

a11y.reducedMotion: A still quarter arc while loading; progress, the check and the cross appear without drawing in.
a11y.screenReader: A progress indicator named by accessibilityLabel. It reports a percentage when given progress, reads Done or Failed when it settles, and announces the result.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { RingSpinner } from '@/components/kinetik/ring-spinner';

<RingSpinner accessibilityLabel="Syncing" status={done ? 'success' : 'loading'} />

// A known amount of work
<RingSpinner accessibilityLabel="Upload" progress={sent / total} />
```

## When to use

- Waits inside a card, a row or a button, where a spinner should also show how it ended.
- Uploads and downloads with a known size, with `progress`.

## When not to use

- Loading whole screens of content. Use Skeleton Sweep.
- Very short waits, under about half a second. Nothing at all feels faster.

## Notes

- The arc grows and shrinks as it turns, and its tail carries over from one cycle to the next, so the motion never jumps.
- Set `status` to `success` or `error` and the ring closes, changes colour and draws a check or a cross. The clock stops then, so a settled spinner costs nothing.
- With reduced motion it shows a still quarter arc while loading, and results appear without drawing in.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add ring-spinner`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
